description.value: The study examined whether Parkinson’s disease is associated with reduced resting-state insula functional connectivity and whether depression in Parkinson’s disease is related to additional connectivity reductions involving the left anterior insula.

design.value: Two groups of PD patients, with and without depression, with 17 participants in each group, and 17 age- and sex-matched normal controls underwent resting-state BOLD fMRI. Seed-based functional connectivity from bilateral anterior and posterior insula regions was compared across groups.

task_description.value: Before scanning, subjects were instructed to relax with their eyes closed without falling asleep, and without directed systematic thought. This was confirmed after completion of scanning.

instrument.value: 3.0T GE MR scanner in the Department of Radiology, Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine

description.value: BOLD images were acquired using an echo planar imaging sequence with TR = 2000 ms, TE = 30 ms, flip angle = 90°, FOV = 240 × 240 mm², matrix = 64 × 64, slice thickness = 5 mm, slice gap = 1 mm, and 23 interleaved axial slices. A total of 185 resting-state BOLD images were acquired from each subject.

Anatomical images were acquired after the functional imaging and consisted of a 3-D GRE T1-weighted sequence with TR/TE = 5.14 ms/1.17 ms, FOV = 240 × 240 mm², matrix = 256 × 256, slice thickness = 1.2 mm, no gap, and 124 sagittal slices.
A T2-weighted imaging sequence was also acquired.
A diffusion tensor imaging sequence was also acquired.
A susceptibility weighted imaging sequence was also acquired.

The first 10 images were excluded. Remaining images were corrected for slice timing using the middle slice as a reference, realigned to remove head motion, regressed for Friston-24 head motion parameters and white matter and CSF signals using CompCor, normalized into standard space using DARTEL, resampled to 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxel size, smoothed with a 6-mm Gaussian kernel, linearly detrended, and bandpass filtered at 0.01–0.1 Hz. Framewise displacement was used to censor time points with FD > 0.5 mm; subjects with fewer than 130 remaining images were excluded.

Subjects whose total length of data was <130 after scrubbing were excluded.

model_settings.value: Pearson’s correlation was calculated between the average time series within each insula ROI and other brain areas. The resulting connectivity maps were transformed to Z maps using Fisher r-to-z transformation.

estimator.value: Pearson’s correlation followed by Fisher r-to-z transformation

model_settings.value: Functional connectivity maps were compared among the three groups, with age and sex used as covariates.
A one-sample t-test was used to demonstrate the connectivity patterns in each group.
Age and FD were compared among the three groups using one-way ANOVA.
A chi-square test was performed to compare sex differences.
Disease duration and scale scores were compared between the two PD groups using two-sample t-test.
Signals from significant clusters were extracted to explore the relationship between insula connectivity and scale scores using partial correlation, with age and sex controlled.
